messages:
sam: quick heads-up — ran a focused nsys sweep on the latest fused-attn change (branch: runtime/fused-attn-experiment). seeing a regression at seq_len=2048, batch=4. nvprof/nsys timeline shows flash_attn variants dominated GPU time and a surprising memcpy in the kv path. attaching snippets below.

sam: nsys summary (trimmed):
```
GPU activities:
 name                           calls  total_ms   avg_ms
 flash_attn_fused_fwd            48    412.3      8.59
 flash_attn_fused_bwd            48    378.9      7.89
 kv_cache_read_kernel            96    145.2      1.51
 memcpy_htod                      6     62.1     10.35
 memcpy_dtoh                      6     58.4      9.73
```

sam: timeline (perfetto/nsys) shows flash_attn kernels are fragmented by frequent small memcpy events that correspond to KV cache flush/refreshs. suspect heuristics are falling back to host copies for alignment when seq_len crosses 1024->2048.

maya: thanks — can you paste the command you used for the run? want to reproduce locally.

sam: sure: 
```
# reproduce
nsys profile --output=prof_seq2048 --trace=nvtx,cuda,osrt --cpuctx --force-overwrite \ 
  --duration=120 --sample=none -- python -m bench.attn_run --model gpt-like --seq 2048 --batch 4 --kv-cache on
```

alex: fwiw we swapped in the fused kernel with a new alignment path that allocates temporary buffers when the kv stride != 32. if the temp_alloc triggers we do host fallback for reads to keep correctness — that might explain memcpys.

jin: I reproduced. small add: capture `cudaMemcpyKind` in the trace. my quick grep on the nsys csv: memcpys are H2D for kv chunk uploads at generation steps 3 and 7. so not pure device-side cacheness issue, more like we trigger partial-host buffering during incremental decode.

maya: hmm. does the old kernel keep everything on-GPU?

jin: old (non-fused) uses per-batch pre-allocated KV buffer sized to max_seq and writes directly in kernel; fused path tries to be memory-frugal and streams sub-blocks, but if sub-blocks misalign we memcpy.

sam: also saw hotspot in kv_cache_read_kernel — lower arithmetic intensity than expected; profile markers show many small reads (lots of L2 thrash). possible pointer aliasing preventing coalesced loads.

alex: two-pronged proposal: 1) change kernel-selection threshold so for decode (batch<=8 and seq>=1024) prefer direct prealloc path; 2) improve streaming path to do device-side padding (round-up) instead of host copy. low risk switch 1 should mitigate most regressions.

maya: agree. also can we add a perf test that runs nsys for seq 128/512/1024/2048 and asserts median token latency? want regression guard.

jin: I'll prototype device-side pad: simple kernel that writes padding zeros into an aligned temp buffer on GPU then run fused_attn over that buffer. should eliminate H2D. I'll push a draft later today.

perf-bot: automated note: created perf issue #987 - "flash-attn fused path triggers host memcpys at seq 2048" and assigned to @jin, @alex, @sam. :white_check_mark:

sam: thanks. last curious point — nvprof showed a surprising amount of time in `cudaLaunchKernel` overhead for many tiny kernels inside flash_attn fused impl. that suggests we might benefit from kernel fusion or batching small warps. any thoughts?

alex: yes, kernel count is high because fused impl breaks down work into many micro-kernels for numerics + attn compute. short term: aggregate micro-kernels for decode case. long term: explore persistent-thread block approach or launch configuration caching to reduce launch overhead.

maya: timeline action items:
- jin: prototype device-side padding and push PR + benchmark (nsys + perfetto traces)
- alex: add kernel-selection heuristic switch + gated rollout (config flag)
- sam: add nsys-based perf test into CI (seq sweep) and attach baseline traces to perf issue

sam: I'll drop the raw prof files into the perf issue: s3://redwood-perf/profiles/1729001234-seq2048/ (contains prof.nsys-rep + perfetto.html).

alex: good. if we can get token latency back within 8% of baseline for seq2048 we're safe to roll. :thumbsup:

maya: perfect. will follow up after PRs land.
